title: Masked Language Modeling
description: Get to know how bidirectional encoders are pretrained by corrupting and reconstructing text.
content:
**Masked language modeling (MLM)** takes the opposite approach to causal LM: corrupt the input, then repair it. **BERT** is an **encoder-only** Transformer trained with MLM - a fraction of tokens (typically 15%) is selected; of these, ~80% are replaced by [MASK], ~10% by a random token, and ~10% are kept unchanged - and the model must reconstruct the originals. Because no causal mask is applied, every masked token is predicted from **bidirectional context**: both left and right neighbors.

BERT also used **Next Sentence Prediction** - deciding whether sentence B actually follows sentence A - to teach sentence-level relations. For downstream use, the **[CLS]** token's final representation feeds a classification head, token-level outputs feed tagging tasks like NER, and sentence pairs are joined with **[SEP]**; a short **fine-tuning** phase on labeled data then adapts the pretrained model - the pretrain-and-fine-tune paradigm.

> Encoder vs decoder at a glance:
> • BERT: bidirectional, MLM, strong at understanding (classification, NER, extractive QA)
> • GPT: causal, next-token prediction, strong at generation
> • Neither is better overall: they optimize different access patterns to context

The limitation of MLM: the [MASK] token never appears in real input at inference, creating a train-test mismatch that causal models avoid.
